feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear positioning for senior digital communications roles and credible progression within one organization. It reads professionally and shows solid scope, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, and there is some redundancy across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility: long tenure at NACo with promotions, large-scale platform work, and relevant tools/platforms signals depth and trustworthiness.  
- Writing is generally polished and specific, especially around web modernization, governance, analytics, and multimedia leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable impact such as growth, engagement improvements, efficiency gains, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; add serial commas consistently in lists (“content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, one or two concrete signals of scale, and slightly less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with current market positioning: “Digital communications and strategy leader” rather than “professional.”
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, analytics, or large-scale mission-driven publishing environments.
- Tighten phrasing by reducing broad lists and emphasizing outcomes-oriented strengths.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, editorial workflow design, and digital governance. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content and aligning stakeholders around effective advocacy and communications strategies.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/system language repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with stronger, CV-aligned phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Prioritize strategic and senior-level capabilities over task-level items; for example, elevate governance, CMS modernization, and digital operations.
- Use parallel noun phrases for consistency and polish.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional alignment • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” repeat Topline Skills/Technical + IT; consider more strategic wording instead.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten around consultant-level impact, transformation outcomes, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and AI-enabled web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4 focused impact bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operations-improvement bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/microsites launched, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search success/engagement lift, stakeholder teams supported.
- Use stronger consultant phrasing: “Designed,” “implemented,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “advised leadership on,” instead of “consult,” “build,” “develop.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and “campaign/storytelling experiences” duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and reserve project specifics for the footer.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize new consulting scope and post-director contributions.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 impact bullets, prioritizing the website migration, analytics buildout, and studio launch.
- Add outcome language where possible: adoption, efficiency gains, reporting speed, production savings, engagement growth, or reduced reliance on vendors.
- Suggested phrasing:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and decision-making.
- Launched NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding advocacy, event, and recurring multimedia production capacity.
- Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to strengthen operational consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep channel management here high-level.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears in the current consulting role; differentiate by emphasizing enterprise leadership and scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing execution scope, cross-functional coordination, and any measurable channel growth or process improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcomes where possible: newsletter open/click rates, audience growth, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or workflow efficiency gains.
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-impact points, e.g. editorial planning across teams, weekly advocacy video production, and workflow/process improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier “Digital Media Manager / Producer” role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/operationalizing the series.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this version focused on execution rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “web modernization,” which better reflects recent senior roles.
- Keep terms parallel in structure; avoid mixing leadership, messaging, and planning language styles.
- If space allows, use “enterprise web modernization” to align with the 10,000+ page Drupal migration and current consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates Core Competencies: “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is very close to Core Competencies: “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they matter for target roles; otherwise trim to avoid diluting recent enterprise Drupal work.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with a clearer outcome-oriented phrase like “Airtable-based workflow systems” or “operational workflow systems.”
- If space allows, use “enterprise web platforms” or “digital platform implementation” to signal leadership, not just hands-on tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; keep here only if shortened.
- WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JS/jQuery are already covered in “Technical + IT.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets for each tool.
- Replace generic items with stronger business-facing terms: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “SEO and digital performance analysis,” “insight-driven optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO and digital performance analysis • Insight-driven optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep tools there and make this section more strategic.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting dashboards” and better matches seniority.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add specificity on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine if Drupal is the lead platform; consider bolding Drupal if formatting allows.
- Add light qualifiers to show depth without repeating experience bullets, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space is tight, drop **GitHub Pages** unless it is materially important to target roles; it reads less strategic than the others.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list broader and this one more tool-specific.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” here since it already appears in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this section should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: APIs, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add level/scope instead of just tools, e.g. “used for CMS customization, campaign microsites, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment workflows”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless important: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner than “HTML5 • CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure elsewhere, so avoid repeating it if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to group by function and highlight stronger tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Drop Basecamp unless it was used recently or materially; it feels older/less relevant than the rest.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the leadership narrative.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of a pure list, e.g. “Workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial planning and cross-team coordination using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack and Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement systems leadership. Since email operations already appear in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-grade platforms over basic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rephrase to signal category and scale: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten naming for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses rather than more tools: **(campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation)**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first; otherwise keep enterprise tools before Mailchimp.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email” is already covered repeatedly in recent work experience; avoid adding claims here unless they introduce distinct technical capability.
- “Engagement” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-focused, not strategic.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and concrete so it reads as the foundation for the leadership roles that follow.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer delivery language: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house communications capacity.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/building the capability, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating “strengthening workflows” if later roles already cover operational improvement in more strategic terms.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation support plus first-of-its-kind multimedia execution.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting program and policy teams, while expanding NACo’s early digital storytelling efforts.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague wording like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with specifics if possible: web features, audio segments, interview production, or policy explainers.
- Add any measurable scope available: number of episodes, audience/listens, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; save team/enterprise-scale language for later positions.
